tables.caption: Table 1. GBFS coverage in the published evaluation [1] and current same-machine regeneration. Paper columns test 90 tasks/domain; ours test 30. Published hmax coverage is not reported. R1 denotes the archived DeepSeek-R1 set.
Table 2. Current experimental contract. Actual run/batch records supersede historical provisional setup prose.
Table 3. Solved counts by domain as easy / medium / hard. Each evaluated tier contains 10 tasks per domain. A dash means not evaluated; IDA* is easy-only.

Table 4. Complete search/heuristic summary (prepared alternate main display). Gap means (%) and optimal fractions use only valid solved tasks with proven positive optima, all easy. IDA* has a 30-task scope; other arms have 90. hmax eligible sets differ.
Table 5. All 17 tasks with proven optimal unit-action cost L*. “Both” means completed A*+hmax and UCS agree; “UCS” means uniform-cost search alone proves the cost. All listed tasks are easy.
Table 6. Matched method/A* medians. Ratios use taskwise pairs solved by both algorithms; n differs by row. IDA* uses only easy tasks. Wall time includes startup, grounding and search.

Table 7. Outcomes in the 780-run matched matrix. Success means a returned plan recorded as valid. There are no invalid-plan, error or exhaustive-unsolved outcomes. Per-arm denominators are 90, except IDA* (30).

embedded_figures.caption: Figure 1. Valid solutions under 60 s and 4096 MiB. The first two panels evaluate four methods on 30 tasks per tier. The right panel compares A* and IDA* on the same 30 easy tasks; IDA* was not tested on medium or hard tasks. Each configuration has one task-seeded run.

Figure 2. Exact gaps use validated plans and proven unit-action optima, all on easy tasks. Left: the identical 17 R1 tasks for every method; black bars show means and labels show optimal/eligible counts. Right: hmax optimal proportions on each method’s own solved, reference-known set. Those sets differ, so the proportions are not a paired ranking.

Figure 4. Matched method/A* ratios in expansions and total wall time. Each point is one task solved by both methods; black ticks show medians, dashed lines show parity and axes are logarithmic. Row labels report pair counts. IDA* uses easy tasks only. These conditional distributions must be read alongside coverage and failures.

Figure 5. Initial-state estimates on 17 easy tasks with proven optimum L*. Dashed lines denote equality and ratio one. Archived R1 overestimates 15/17 states, with median ratio 1.18 and maximum 2.10; hmax overestimates 0/17. Ranked curves sort tasks independently within each heuristic. These are initial states, not the pending reachable-state sample.
